coding.case_type: Federal employment (MSPB, arbitrator, OCWR, back-pay claims)

issues.description: Whistleblower reprisal under WPA: Board found Khaghani's procurement disclosure (Disclosure 2) was not protected because he lacked a reasonable belief of wrongdoing; court rejected challenge to that legal standard
issues.quote: We see no such error in the AJ's decision.

issues.description: Agency's clear and convincing evidence defense that it would have taken the same personnel actions absent protected disclosures (non-selection and SNR training removal); court upheld Board's Carr factor analysis and credibility findings
issues.quote: The Board reasonably found that the Department would have taken the same personnel actions in the absence of Mr. Khaghani's protected disclosures.

issues.description: Challenge that the Board failed to sufficiently explain its credibility determinations and reasoning; court found the agency explanation adequate
issues.quote: Mr. Khaghani fails to explain how the Board deviated from the correct legal standard or misapplied it.

coding.author: PER CURIAM
coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition affirming MSPB denial of IRA corrective action. Court treated the clear-and-convincing defense and the reasonable-belief standard as merits questions under E03. The significant-change and cumulative-effect arguments were folded into E03 analysis rather than coded separately. No dissents.

coding.side_a_parties: Ziklag IP LLC (successor plaintiff to Touchmusic Entertainment LLC)
coding.side_b_parties: Apple Inc.; Amazon Web Services, Inc.

issues.description: Collateral estoppel: the Netflix district court's determination that Touchmusic retained the right to sue for past damages (not assigned to Ziklag) precludes Ziklag from relitigating that issue on appeal in the Apple and Amazon cases; invoked by the accused infringers.
issues.quote: Accordingly, all collateral estoppel factors are satisfied.

coding.author: Stoll
coding.notes: Ziklag's merits argument on whether the assignment conveyed the right to sue for past infringement was not reached; the court held it precluded by the Netflix ruling, so no P20 ownership merits issue was coded. Jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. 1295(a)(1) was a routine statement and was not coded. Nonprecedential disposition; no dissent.

coding.side_a_parties: Ziklag IP LLC (successor to Touchmusic Entertainment LLC), plaintiff-appellant

issues.description: Denial of leave to amend to re-substitute Touchmusic as plaintiff under Rules 15(a) and 17(a)(3), which the court held was not an abuse of discretion because the substitution was made in bad faith for tactical advantage; the dismissal with prejudice was affirmed.
issues.quote: Accordingly, even considering Rule 15(a), the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying Ziklag leave to amend its complaint.

coding.author: Stoll
coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition on appeal from N.D. Ill. (No. 1:24-cv-01789, Rowland, J.). The only issue decided was abuse of discretion in denying leave to amend to re-substitute the plaintiff; Ziklag did not challenge the finding that Touchmusic retained the right to sue for past damages. Ziklag's notice argument and Rule 15 framework argument were rejected on the merits, so they are not coded separately. Standard of review was Seventh Circuit law, applied because the issue is not unique to patent law.

issues.description: Construction of the claim term 'a starting time-frequency coordinate' as requiring a single value rather than separate time and frequency coordinates; Board construction affirmed, favoring the patent owner.
issues.quote: The claims of the '450 patent require that the starting point of a segment of time-frequency resource be specified by a single value, not by separate time and frequency values.

issues.description: Petitioners forfeited their challenge to the Board's finding that Vijayan089 fails to disclose the claimed limitation by raising it only in the reply brief and not developing it in the opening brief.
issues.quote: In this circumstance, petitioners have not preserved an argument that the Board reversibly erred in its reading of Vijayan089.

coding.author: Taranto
coding.notes: Nonprecedential Federal Circuit affirmance of a joint final written decision in three IPRs. No dissent. Chief Judge Moore and Judge Prost joined. The court did not reach the Board's separate timeliness ruling on a Vijayan089 modification argument, so it is not coded.
